title: A*: heuristic reliability and route evaluation
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: admissible — Heuristic never overestimates the true cheapest remaining cost.
consistent — Heuristic obeys h(u) ≤ edge(u,v)+h(v) for every edge.
suboptimal — A valid route whose cost is greater than the cheapest possible.
heuristic — An estimated remaining cost used to guide search.

blocks.title: Find the real remaining cost
blocks.text: From A, the cheapest route A→B→G costs 2+2=4. Therefore h(A)=3 is admissible, but h(A)=9 is not.

blocks.title: Safe estimates support optimal search
blocks.text: With h(A)=3, A is expanded before B, improving the route to B and finally G at cost 6.

blocks.title: Watch the misleading estimate
blocks.text: With h(A)=9, A has f=11; B has f=7 and leads to goal at cost 8.

blocks.title: Why the error matters
blocks.text: A* that stops on the first goal removed from the open set can return this 8-cost path before exploring A, even though a 6-cost route exists.

blocks.title: Worked example · Predict the choice
blocks.text: V has g1,h3,f4; W has g5,h1,f6. Expand V.

blocks.title: Predict the choice
blocks.text: After M, O has f5+1=6; N has f2+7=9, so O is selected.

blocks.title: Review the choice
blocks.text: O reaches G at g7,f7. G is selected before N, so the early-goal algorithm returns cost 7.

blocks.title: Review the choice
blocks.text: But M→N→O→G costs 2+2+2=6; the bad h(N)=7 overestimates N's true remaining cost 4.

blocks.title: Review the choice
blocks.text: Using an admissible estimate such as h(N)=3 allows the cheaper path to be found.
